passages.p1: Read the email from Eve to her grandpa. Choose the correct word for each gap. The first one is done for you. Dear Grandpa, This afternoon I went for a [[1]] in the park. The [[2]] were green and full of flowers. I sat down on a wooden [[3]] to rest. Some children were playing on the [[4]]. I gave some bread to the [[5]] on the lake. The park was so [[6]] and beautiful today.
passages.p2: Put the sentences in the correct order to make a story. The first one is done for you.
passages.p3:
A. For most of human history, children did not have toys bought from shops. They made their own games using sticks, stones and whatever they could find outside.

B. In many farming families, children were expected to help from a very young age, feeding animals or collecting water long before they went to school.

C. The invention of cheap printing meant that, for the first time, ordinary families could buy books written specially for young readers.

D. When radios appeared in most homes, children would gather every evening to listen to adventure programmes made just for them.

E. Later, television changed everything, and many parents began to worry that their sons and daughters spent too many hours sitting in front of a screen.

F. Today, much of children's play has moved online, and friends who live far apart can now build worlds together in the same computer game.

G. Yet many experts remind us that running, climbing and playing outside are still the healthiest activities of all for a growing child.

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

The old houses in this town _____ very beautiful a hundred years ago.
questions.explanation:
Quá khứ đơn 'were' diễn tả đặc điểm của một sự việc lịch sử đã hoàn toàn thuộc về quá khứ.
[TD]Dịch: Những ngôi nhà cũ trong thị trấn này rất đẹp một trăm năm trước.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Many people have objected _____ the new rule.
questions.explanation:
Cụm động từ + giới từ cố định: 'object to' nghĩa là phản đối.
[TD]Dịch: Nhiều người đã phản đối quy định mới.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Oh, _____ Tom tonight — shall I tell him?
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại tiếp diễn 'I'm seeing' diễn tả cuộc hẹn đã sắp xếp ở tương lai gần.
[TD]Dịch: À, tối nay tôi có hẹn gặp Tom — tôi nhắn anh ấy nhé?[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

There was _____ wood in the box, so the carpenters had to suspend the renovation.
questions.explanation:
Wood' là danh từ không đếm được nên dùng 'little' (rất ít) chứ không phải 'few'.
[TD]Dịch: Trong hộp có rất ít gỗ nên thợ mộc phải tạm hoãn việc cải tạo.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You should bring an umbrella; _____, you will get wet.
questions.explanation:
Otherwise' (nếu không thì) nối hai mệnh đề, nêu hậu quả nếu không làm điều trước đó.
[TD]Dịch: Bạn nên mang theo ô; nếu không, bạn sẽ bị ướt.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

This is the third time I _____ to call you today.
questions.explanation:
This is the third time...' đi với hiện tại hoàn thành 'have tried' để chỉ chuỗi hành động tính đến hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: Đây là lần thứ ba tôi cố gọi cho bạn hôm nay.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If I _____ you, I wouldn't be signing that contract without thorough legal advice.
questions.explanation:
Câu điều kiện loại 2, sau 'If I' dùng 'were' cho mọi ngôi để diễn tả giả định không có thật ở hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ không ký hợp đồng đó mà không có tư vấn pháp lý kỹ lưỡng.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

When the teacher came, the boys _____ have run away already.
questions.explanation:
Could have + V3' diễn tả khả năng có thể đã xảy ra trong quá khứ.
[TD]Dịch: Khi cô giáo đến, mấy cậu bé có thể đã chạy đi mất rồi.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

After a long talk, they finally _____ on going to the beach.
questions.explanation:
Cấu trúc 'agree on + V-ing' diễn tả nhất trí về việc làm gì.
[TD]Dịch: Sau một hồi nói chuyện dài, cuối cùng họ nhất trí đi biển.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ fire, please use the stairs, not the elevator.
questions.explanation:
In case of + danh từ' (trong trường hợp) đi với danh từ, khác 'in case' đi với mệnh đề.
[TD]Dịch: Trong trường hợp có hỏa hoạn, hãy dùng cầu thang bộ, không dùng thang máy.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Don't worry — we _____ the work on time, I promise.
questions.explanation:
Will' diễn tả dự đoán mang tính cam kết, khẳng định chắc chắn về tương lai.
[TD]Dịch: Đừng lo — chúng tôi sẽ hoàn thành công việc đúng hạn, tôi hứa.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Scientists said last week that they _____ a new type of fish in the deep sea.
questions.explanation:
Hiện tại hoàn thành 'have discovered' vì kết quả còn giá trị hiện tại.
[TD]Dịch: Tuần trước các nhà khoa học nói rằng họ đã phát hiện một loại cá mới ở biển sâu.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

His words _____ anger among the listeners.
questions.explanation:
Chủ ngữ 'words' tự gây ra hành động nên dùng thể chủ động 'provoked'.
[TD]Dịch: Lời nói của anh ấy đã gây ra sự tức giận trong người nghe.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She wrote her best songs during a time when she _____ from a broken heart.
questions.explanation:
Quá khứ tiếp diễn 'was suffering' diễn tả tình trạng kéo dài làm bối cảnh cho hành động 'wrote'.
[TD]Dịch: Cô ấy viết những bài hát hay nhất trong thời gian cô đang chịu nỗi đau thất tình.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Direct: 'This bag of mine is very old.' Reported: She said that _____ was very old.
questions.explanation:
Tường thuật đổi 'this...of mine' thành 'that...of hers' theo ngôi và khoảng cách.
[TD]Dịch: Cô ấy nói rằng cái túi đó của cô ấy rất cũ.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

She _____ ever turns down an invitation to perform at a charity event.
questions.explanation:
Hardly' (hầu như không) đứng trước 'ever' tạo cụm chỉ tần suất; 'hard' lại nghĩa khác.
[TD]Dịch: Cô ấy hầu như không bao giờ từ chối lời mời biểu diễn tại sự kiện từ thiện.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I _____ as well stay home. There is nothing to do outside.
questions.explanation:
May as well' gợi ý nên làm điều gì đó vì chẳng có lý do gì để không làm.
[TD]Dịch: Tôi cũng nên ở nhà thôi. Bên ngoài chẳng có gì để làm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ when his colleagues asked him to lead the project.
questions.explanation:
Sau 'hardly' đầu câu phải đảo ngữ: trợ động từ 'had' đứng trước chủ ngữ.
[TD]Dịch: Marcus vừa mới đồng ý thì các đồng nghiệp đã đề nghị anh dẫn dắt dự án.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

You'd better take a portable charger _____ the battery dies during the expedition.
questions.explanation:
In case' nêu sự đề phòng (phòng khi), khác với điều kiện 'if'.
[TD]Dịch: Bạn nên mang theo bộ sạc dự phòng phòng khi pin hết trong chuyến thám hiểm.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

If only I _____ harder for the test, my score would be better now.
questions.explanation:
If only' + 'had + V3' diễn tả tiếc nuối về quá khứ trong câu điều kiện hỗn hợp.
[TD]Dịch: Giá mà tôi đã học chăm hơn cho bài thi, điểm của tôi bây giờ đã tốt hơn.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

I'll have a quiet word with Margaret when she _____ from her sales trip to Singapore.
questions.explanation:
Trong mệnh đề thời gian sau 'when', dùng hiện tại đơn 'returns' để chỉ tương lai.
[TD]Dịch: Tôi sẽ nói nhỏ với Margaret khi cô ấy trở về từ chuyến công tác bán hàng ở Singapore.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Nothing of _____ interest happened during the entire trustees' meeting.
questions.explanation:
Cụm 'of interest' đi với danh từ trừu tượng không đếm được nên dùng zero article (không mạo từ).
[TD]Dịch: Không có gì đáng chú ý xảy ra trong suốt cuộc họp của ban quản trị.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ you possibly close that window? There's a rather chilly draught coming through.
questions.explanation:
Dùng 'Could' để đưa ra lời yêu cầu lịch sự.
[TD]Dịch: Liệu bạn có thể đóng giúp cửa sổ kia không? Có một luồng gió khá lạnh lùa vào.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

Iron is not _____ valuable as platinum, but it has far more industrial uses.
questions.explanation:
Cấu trúc phủ định 'not so...as' (không...bằng) dùng 'so' thay cho 'as' ở vế đầu.
[TD]Dịch: Sắt không có giá trị bằng bạch kim, nhưng nó có nhiều công dụng công nghiệp hơn nhiều.[/TD]

questions.content:
Grammar and Vocabulary — Grammar

_____ the firefighters, the house would have burned down completely.
questions.explanation:
But for + danh từ' nghĩa là 'nếu không nhờ', thay cho mệnh đề điều kiện.
[TD]Dịch: Nếu không nhờ lính cứu hỏa, ngôi nhà đã cháy rụi hoàn toàn.[/TD]

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Could you tell me about your best friend?
questions.sampleAnswer: My best friend is Lan. We studied together at secondary school, and now we live near each other. She is kind, funny and very helpful. I can talk to her when I feel sad. We are close because she understands me and always gives me good advice.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

What are you planning to do this coming weekend?
questions.sampleAnswer: This coming weekend, I am going to visit my grandparents with my parents. They live in a small town about one hour from my house. We will have lunch together and talk. On Sunday, I want to clean my room and prepare my lessons for next week.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 1 - Personal information

Do you like going to the cinema? Why or why not?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I like going to the cinema because the screen is big and the sound is very good. I usually go with my sister or my friends once a month. We often watch comedy films. It is fun to eat popcorn and enjoy the film together.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Describe the picture.
questions.sampleAnswer: In this picture, I can see the inside of a cinema. It is quite dark, but the light from the screen is on the people’s faces. There are four young adults, two women and two men. They are sitting next to each other in comfortable cinema seats and they are watching a film. They are wearing casual clothes, such as T-shirts and jackets. The man in the middle is holding a large bucket of popcorn on his lap. The other people are looking at the screen. They are smiling and their faces look excited. I think they are watching a funny action film or a new comedy. They seem to be having a very good time together.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

What is your favourite type of film or movie, and why?
questions.sampleAnswer: My favourite type of film is comedy. I like comedy films because they make me laugh and help me forget stress after work or school. I usually watch them with my sister at home on Friday evenings. My favourite actor is Mr Bean because he is very funny, even when he does not say much. I feel happier after watching a good comedy.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 2 - Describe a picture

Why do many people nowadays realise the importance of entertainment and relaxation in their lives?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think many people understand that entertainment and relaxation are important because modern life is busy and stressful. They work, study and use phones all day. After that, they need time to rest their minds and bodies. Watching a film, listening to music or playing sport can help them feel calm. When people relax, they can sleep better and do their work better the next day.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Compare these two pictures.
questions.sampleAnswer:
In the first picture, I can see a small street food stall by the road. The owner is cooking and serving food from a cart. Two customers are eating nearby. They look relaxed, and the place is busy and lively. It is outdoors, so people can watch the traffic and talk to other customers.

In the second picture, there is a smart restaurant indoors. A waiter is serving one customer at a table with a white tablecloth. The room looks quiet, clean, and expensive. The customer is dressed nicely.

The street stall is probably much cheaper than the restaurant. Students and workers may eat at the stall, but couples or business people may choose the restaurant. I feel more comfortable at a street stall because it is casual, friendly, and I can eat quickly.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Do you like eating out alone? Why or why not?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I like eating out alone sometimes. It is quiet, and I can choose any food I want. I often go to a small café near my house on Sunday morning. I drink coffee and read messages on my phone. I do not feel lonely because I enjoy my own time. But for dinner, I usually prefer eating with my family or friends.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 3 - Compare two pictures

Do you think keeping up social relationships is important?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think keeping social relationships is very important. Friends and family can help us when we have problems, and they make life happier. For example, I call my mother every evening, even when I am busy. I also meet my old school friends once a month. We talk, eat together, and laugh. These relationships help me feel supported and less stressed.

questions.content:
Speaking — Part 4 - Discuss an abstract topic

Tell me about a time when you tried an activity high above the ground at an amusement park.
questions.sampleAnswer: Last summer I went to an amusement park with my friends. There was a high ropes course in the park, and I decided to try it. First, a staff member gave me a helmet and a harness. Then I climbed a tall wooden pole and I walked across a rope bridge. It was very high, maybe ten metres above the ground. In the middle I stopped and I could not move. My legs were shaking. My friends shouted my name, so I walked slowly to the end. After that, I felt very happy and proud. When I am high up and I cannot come down, I feel nervous and my heart beats fast. But I also feel excited. I think adventure activities are good for children, but they must be safe. Children need a helmet, a harness and an adult with them. Then it is fun, not dangerous.
